key_insight: Kidney-adapted AI predicted spatial gene expression from routine histology, linking tissue features to injury, repair, and fibrosis-associated molecular programs.
clinical_relevance: This kidney disease study—not cancer drug discovery—could extend molecular characterization to archived biopsies, but does not establish clinical diagnostic utility.
method: Adapted DeepSpot-M using paired histology and spatial transcriptomics from 209 KPMP participants.
Evaluated predictions in held-out human biopsies and 567 rats with defined nephrotoxin exposures.
Generated 5.46 million virtual spots from 1,534 slides covering 476 additional KPMP participants.
evidence_signal: Mean gene-expression prediction correlation improved from 0.22 to 0.43 for each model’s 1,000 best-predicted genes; predictions preserved all 13 disease-marker differences and all 11 measured associations with eGFR.
watch_item: Predicted expression is not a direct molecular measurement; broader validation is needed before clinical use.
paper_title: Virtual spatial transcriptomics links kidney histopathology to disease-associated molecular programs
